headline: Plane drops 14,000ft after co-pilot stabs captain in cockpit struggle
summary: A flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv plunged thousands of feet when a co-pilot attacked the captain, forcing passengers to storm the cockpit to regain control.
details: A flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv plunged more than 14,000 feet in 30 seconds after a violent struggle in the cockpit, according to Israeli officials.
Israeli officials stated that the co-pilot stabbed the captain, who was left bloodied on the floor, in an attempt to crash the aircraft carrying over 170 Israelis.
The wounded captain used his remaining energy to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew members to rush in and overpower the attacker.
A reserve flydubai crew on board took control of the aircraft and landed it safely at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia.
Flight tracking data from flightradar24 showed the plane cruising at 34,000 feet before the sudden drop and a detour into Jordanian airspace before returning to Saudi Arabia.
While Israeli officials have detailed the attack, flydubai has stated that the underlying reasons for the event remain unknown and warned against premature speculation.
caption:
A plane plunged 14,000 feet in 30 seconds after a co-pilot stabbed the captain. Passengers had to storm the cockpit to save the flight.

A flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv plunged more than 14,000 feet in 30 seconds after a violent struggle in the cockpit, according to Israeli officials.

Israeli officials stated that the co-pilot stabbed the captain, who was left bloodied on the floor, in an attempt to crash the aircraft carrying over 170 Israelis.

The wounded captain used his remaining energy to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew members to rush in and overpower the attacker.

A reserve flydubai crew on board took control of the aircraft and landed it safely at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia.

Flight tracking data from flightradar24 showed the plane cruising at 34,000 feet before the sudden drop and a detour into Jordanian airspace before returning to Saudi Arabia.

While Israeli officials have detailed the attack, flydubai has stated that the underlying reasons for the event remain unknown and warned against premature speculation.

headline: PM Tarique Rahman orders release of teacher detained over alleged remarks
summary: The Prime Minister directed police to release a Kushtia teacher with dignity after he was detained for allegedly making derogatory comments about the PM's pronunciation.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has directed police to release a school teacher in Kushtia who was detained for allegedly making derogatory remarks about him.
The teacher, Golam Kibria Lalon, teaches Bangla at Pragpur Secondary School in Daulatpur upazila, and was detained by police on Wednesday.
The incident began on Tuesday when students alleged that Lalon commented on the PM's Bangla pronunciation in a recent UN General Assembly speech and made objectionable remarks.
Following these allegations, students and guardians gathered at the school on Wednesday morning, demanding action against the teacher.
PM's adviser Mahdi Amin stated that the PM was upset to learn of the detention and instructed the police to ensure the teacher's safe return home.
The Prime Minister emphasized that freedom of expression should be respected even when others disagree, calling it a strength of democracy.
Headteacher Ashrafuzzaman Mukul noted that the teacher denied making the derogatory remarks during questioning.
Daulatpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Khaledur Rahman confirmed that the incident had created tension in the area.
caption:
A teacher was detained for allegedly criticizing the PM's pronunciation—but the PM himself ordered his release.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has directed police to release a school teacher in Kushtia who was detained for allegedly making derogatory remarks about him.

The teacher, Golam Kibria Lalon, teaches Bangla at Pragpur Secondary School in Daulatpur upazila, and was detained by police on Wednesday.

The incident began on Tuesday when students alleged that Lalon commented on the PM's Bangla pronunciation in a recent UN General Assembly speech and made objectionable remarks.

Following these allegations, students and guardians gathered at the school on Wednesday morning, demanding action against the teacher.

PM's adviser Mahdi Amin stated that the PM was upset to learn of the detention and instructed the police to ensure the teacher's safe return home.

The Prime Minister emphasized that freedom of expression should be respected even when others disagree, calling it a strength of democracy.

Headteacher Ashrafuzzaman Mukul noted that the teacher denied making the derogatory remarks during questioning.

Daulatpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Khaledur Rahman confirmed that the incident had created tension in the area.
